name: Migvora
author: Yavuz Selim

sections.description:
Migvora backs up your entire WordPress site – database, media, themes, plugins and language files – into a single portable .migvora file. Import that file on any WordPress site (even a brand-new one) and Migvora puts everything back, replaces the old domain with the new one and refreshes permalinks. No FTP, no phpMyAdmin, no search-replace scripts.

Why Migvora?

  • One-click full backup – database + files, or database only / files only.
  • Smart domain replacement – http → https, www, sub-folders and a different table prefix are handled automatically. Serialized and JSON data stay intact, and domains inside file names are left alone.
  • Safe by design – the import goes into temporary tables and is switched live in one atomic step at the very end. A restore point is created first, and “Undo last import” takes you back in one click.
  • Built for big sites – work runs in small chunks, so it never hits the PHP time limit. Close the tab and it carries on where it stopped.
  • Maintenance mode – visitors see a clean maintenance page while an import runs.
  • Size and time estimate before you start, plus folder and table exclusions.
  • Large downloads – multi-gigabyte backups download reliably (resumable links).
  • System check – PHP limits, disk space, cron, LiteSpeed and nginx settings on one screen, with one-click fixes.
  • Turkish and English interface – switch the language right in the plugin header.

Free version

Everything in this plugin is free and works without an account or a license: full and partial restore, encrypted (AES-256) backups and imports of any size. Backups are taken manually and kept on your server.

Migvora Premium

Migvora Premium is a separate add-on plugin, sold outside WordPress.org, for site owners and agencies that need more:

  • Direct site-to-site transfer (no download and re-upload)
  • Google Drive, Amazon S3 / Cloudflare R2 / S3-compatible storage and FTP/SFTP
  • Scheduled backups and automatic backups before updates
  • E-mail and Telegram notifications
  • Shareable download links

Premium is not required for anything the free version does.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins → Add New, search for Migvora and click Install Now, then Activate.
  2. Open Migvora in the admin menu.
  3. Create Backup → choose what to include → Start. Download the .migvora file when it is done.
  4. On the new site: install Migvora, go to Import, upload the file and follow the steps.

Very large backup files can also be copied into wp-content/wpsfm-storage/backups/ by FTP/SSH; they then appear on the Import page.
sections.faq:
Is there a size limit?

No. Creating and importing backups has no size limit in Migvora. Only your server’s disk space and PHP settings matter; work runs in small chunks, and very large files can be copied into the backups folder by FTP/SSH.

Why is there a migvora-memory.php file in mu-plugins?

Migvora versions 2.11.2 to 2.11.4 could add this small file to raise the PHP memory limit of migrated sites. Current versions never add or copy any file to mu-plugins. If the file is still on your site, you can remove it on Migvora → System (“Remove Memory File”) or simply delete it. To raise the memory limit, use your hosting panel (php.ini / PHP settings); the System page shows the lines to use.

Will my site break if an import fails?

No. The backup is imported into temporary tables and only switched live in a single atomic RENAME TABLE at the very end. Any failure before that leaves the site as it was. A restore point is created before every import.

Does it change links when I move to a new domain?

Yes. Old addresses (http, https, www, sub-folders) are replaced with the new ones in every table, including serialized and JSON data. Permalinks and .htaccess are refreshed after the import.

Where are backups stored?

In wp-content/wpsfm-storage/backups/, outside the plugin folder, so updating or removing the plugin never deletes them. The folder is protected from direct web access (.htaccess, web.config, random file names for nginx).

Why do I have to log in again after an import?

The database – including users – now comes from the backup. Log in with the username and password of the site the backup was taken from.

Does it support Multisite?

Not yet. Single-site installations are fully supported.

Which servers does it work on?

Any server with PHP 7.4 or later: cPanel, Plesk, CloudPanel, DirectAdmin, LiteSpeed, nginx and Apache. The System page shows possible problems and fixes most of them in one click.

Does the free version connect to external services?

No. The free version does not send any data anywhere; backups stay on your server. It only contains links to migvora.tr (plans and documentation). Premium features that use third-party services (Google Drive, Amazon S3, Telegram, the license server) are part of the separate Migvora Premium plugin and are documented there.
sections.changelog:
2.11.5

  • The optional memory booster was removed: Migvora no longer adds or copies any file to wp-content/mu-plugins. A file left there by versions 2.11.2–2.11.4 can be removed on Migvora → System.
  • Removed an unnecessary include of wp-admin/includes/misc.php on the System page.

2.11.4

  • The memory booster (wp-content/mu-plugins/migvora-memory.php) is no longer added automatically after an import. It is a complete file shipped with the plugin (mu-loader/) and is copied only when an administrator clicks “Install Memory Booster” on Migvora → System, after an explanation. It can be removed with one click.

2.11.3

  • Fix: the Logs page used str_contains() (PHP 8 only) and failed on PHP 7.4.
  • Settings: only the known, sanitized cloud destination fields are passed to the migvora_save_settings hook (no raw $_POST).

2.11.2

  • Fix: imports stopped at “Domain / path replacement” with “Invalid utf8mb4 character string” on sites with binary columns (for example Wordfence’s wffilemods table).
  • After an import, if the new server’s PHP memory_limit is below 1024M, Migvora adds a small must-use plugin (wp-content/mu-plugins/migvora-memory.php) that raises it, so page builders such as Elementor Pro do not run out of memory on the new host.

2.11.1

  • Partial restore, encrypted backups and imports of any size are now part of the free plugin (no license needed).
  • Maintenance page styles are loaded through the WordPress styles API.
  • Stricter validation of server variables and the HTTP Range header.
  • Removed the unneeded load_plugin_textdomain() call.

2.11.0

  • First release on WordPress.org.
  • Full-site backup and restore with automatic domain replacement (serialized-safe).
  • Atomic switch with restore point and “Undo last import”.
  • Chunked engine for large sites, maintenance mode during imports.
  • Size and time estimate, folder and table exclusions, system check.
  • Turkish and English interface.

upgrade_notice.2.11.4: The memory booster is now installed only on request from Migvora → System (never automatically).
upgrade_notice.2.11.3: PHP 7.4 fix for the Logs page and stricter input handling on the Settings page.
upgrade_notice.2.11.2: Fixes imports of sites with binary database columns (Wordfence) and raises the PHP memory limit of migrated sites when it is too low.
